title: High and low
summary: Every key plays a note, and every note has a pitch: how high or low it sounds.

steps.title: Every key plays a note
steps.body:
Press any key and you hear a **note**: one musical sound. A tune is notes one after another. When you press several keys at once, you hear several notes together.

**Why it matters:** Music theory is about notes: which ones, how far apart they are, and how they fit together. When your band says "hit that note again", this is what they mean.

steps.title: High and low
steps.body:
How high or low a note sounds is its **pitch**. On a piano, pitch rises as you move to the right and falls as you move to the left.

**Why it matters:** Musicians say a tune goes "up" or "down". On the keyboard, up always means to the right and down always means to the left, so you can follow those directions straight away.

steps.title: Right is higher
steps.body: The key on the right has a higher pitch than the key on the left. Play them both and listen.

items.prompt: Play the lit key. It is further right, so its pitch is higher.
Play the lit key. It is further left, so its pitch is lower.

steps.title: Up and down
steps.body: Play any tune you know. Notice how your hand moves right when the tune goes up, and left when it comes down.

items.prompt: Two keys are lit. Which one has the higher pitch?
Two keys are lit. Which one has the lower pitch?
Two keys are lit. Which one has the higher pitch?
